title: E1: exact techniques without retrieval, P(technique) = P(family) x P(technique | family), answer from the top three families
question: Does the family head with a within-family technique head, trained jointly on F2's data, name the exact ATT&CK technique more often than the retrieve-then-pick models and Jev, above all on CTI-HAL?

design.heads: F2's family head (cosine over 222 families) plus a technique head (cosine over the 697 listed techniques, rows initialised from each technique's own 'label: cut description' state, centred on their mean). P(technique | family) is a softmax of the technique logits within the family's parent and sub-techniques; a family's parent is its own option ('family only'), and a family without sub-techniques has P = 1
design.answer: the most probable technique by P(family) x P(technique | family) among the 3 most probable families (owner's choice 2026-10-14: a hard limit to the top family caps exact accuracy at family top-1, dev 0.73-0.76, while the top three cover 0.87-0.91)
design.loss: per example: F2's family cross-entropy + 1.0 x the mean over gold techniques of -log P(gold technique | its family); the technique term is skipped for AnnoCTR rows (parent-level links by convention: 1% of AnnoCTR train labels are sub-techniques) and for gold ids outside the catalogue

data.train: F2's rows unchanged: cases_train.jsonl 6,308 + cases_annoctr_train.jsonl 1,453 + cases_attack_train.jsonl 16,273 = 24,034 rows; exact targets on every row except the 1,453 AnnoCTR rows (labels with a sub-technique: public train 42%, ATT&CK procedures 54%)
data.dev: public dev (659; 32% sub-technique labels) for exact top-1; AnnoCTR dev (336; parent-level labels) for family top-1 only
data.confirmation: CTI-HAL 968 (laptop), public test 1,391, AnnoCTR test 738 (family top-1 only, its labels are parent-level)

fixed.init: cribl-ai/cribl-decision-1.0 adapter and freshly initialised heads, as F2 (not F2's checkpoint)
fixed.training: as F2: LoRA lr 1e-4, head lr 1e-3 for both heads, 16 examples per step and per forward pass, cosine, 3% warmup, seed 7, 2 epochs, a checkpoint every quarter epoch (8 + step 0); no definition rows, no margin
fixed.compute: RunPod secure RTX 4090 (no CTI-HAL uploaded; the selected checkpoint is scored on CTI-HAL on the laptop)

selection: the highest mean of public dev exact top-1 and AnnoCTR dev family top-1; ties the earlier

baselines_already_measured.note: B1/B3 under never-abstain (parent prereg amendment 4); the pipeline's top 10 holds the exact gold on 74.1% of CTI-HAL and 80.5% of public test, which caps the retrieve-then-pick models and Jev

success.headline: CTI-HAL exact top-1: E1 minus B3 (same 968 statements, B3 never-abstain), paired 95% CI lower bound above 0
secondary: CTI-HAL exact top-1: E1 minus Jev C1 as reported, CI lower bound above 0
public test exact top-1: E1 minus B1 (never-abstain), CI lower bound above 0
success.reported: exact top-1 with the top family only and with every family; exact top-3/5; exact top-1 for gold sub-techniques and for parent-only labels; ECE of the exact answer; family top-1 against F2 on all three sets (does the technique task cost family accuracy?); against pipeline rank-1 and Jev never-abstain; every checkpoint's dev curve

stop_rules: more than 1% of a split's cases end in error
confirmation_runs: the selected checkpoint once on CTI-HAL, public test and AnnoCTR test; nothing is chosen, refit or rerun because of a confirmation result
adoption: none: an experiment, no product wiring
informed_by: F1-F3 results (docs 21.3.18); F2's dev family top-1/2/3/5 (public dev 0.730/0.821/0.866/0.906, AnnoCTR dev 0.756/0.872/0.908/0.949); the share of labels that name a sub-technique per set (counted on labels only, CTI-HAL included: 45%); the baselines above (already reported in docs 21.3.18); a laptop pilot (100 train rows, 30 dev cases; mechanics only: trains, saves, reloads, scores). No E1 model exists.
